subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - FastPay (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Autoscale SLO qualification - FastPay (post-call recap)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we pull together an SLO/benchmark plan.

Recap of what you asked us to qualify:
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 1200 ms (for full-response generation)
- Throughput: steady-state ~50 req/s, expected peak bursts up to 150 req/s (marketing spikes)
- Concurrency: ~40-60 concurrent sessions, with occasional bursts to ~120
- Streaming: yes — partial token streaming required for progressive UX (users expect first tokens within 200–300ms)
- Payload/response size: avg response ~180 tokens, worst-case ~600 tokens

Autoscale / burst capacity constraints you highlighted:
- Need predictable warm pool behavior for marketing bursts (scale-up time target <= 90s to absorb 2–3x traffic)
- Prefer limited queueing (don’t want users to wait >30s)
- Warm pools preferred over cold starts for tail latency guarantees

What I’ll deliver next:
1) SLO worksheet with the above numbers and a few proposed config variants (attached: redwood-slo-worksheet.xlsx)
2) Autoscale config proposal (warm pool sizes, scale-up time targets, queue sizing) — draft attached
3) A short benchmark plan and a proposed 60-minute soak/scale test window where Redwood runs with a copy of your traffic profile

Asks for you — please send the traffic CSV (sample 24h aggregate with peak 1m/5m buckets) and confirm the procurement contact so we can include pricing and any contracting notes.

Next steps / proposed schedule:
- You send traffic sample + procurement contact by EOD Fri 7/2
- We send back SLO worksheet + autoscale proposal by Mon 7/5
- Align on a 60-minute benchmark window (we can run Wed 7/7 or Thu 7/8)

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering (Ben & Dylan) for the benchmark design.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-slo-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), autoscale-config-proposal.pdf (draft)

Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - FastPay (post-call recap)

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap, that matches our discussion. A few clarifications and answers:
- Confirming SLO targets: p95 250ms, p99 1200ms (we can be flexible on p99 for very large responses but want to understand typical tails)
- Traffic: our typical steady-state is ~45–55 req/s; marketing campaigns create short spikes to ~140–160 req/s for 10–20 minute windows
- Concurrency: typical 50, but bursts to ~120 is accurate
- Streaming: required. UX team expects first token within ~250ms of request so initial token latency is important.

I attached the traffic export (traffic-patterns.csv) — it has 24h buckets plus a 1m granularity sample for the last campaign. Procurement copied to loop in contracting.

Two asks:
1) Can you call out the queueing behavior in the proposal (e.g., how long requests sit in the router queue under different configs and when we start getting 429s)?
2) Can you estimate the warm pool size needed to meet p95 during a 3x burst (we’re happy for Redwood to recommend conservative numbers and we can iterate after the benchmark)

We’re aiming to get pricing + SOW rolling next week if the benchmark looks good.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Principal Product Manager, ML Platform | FastPay
alex.chen@fastpay.com

Attachment: traffic-patterns.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO qualification - FastPay (post-call recap)

Alex —

Appreciate the traffic file — that helps a lot. I attached a filled-in SLO worksheet and a draft autoscale config (autoscale-config-proposal.pdf). High level summary of our recommendations based on the traffic:

Recommended config (initial):
- Baseline warm pool: 6 warm workers (each worker ~1 GPU vCPU bundle for the model you described) — covers ~2x your steady-state with headroom
- Burst target: ability to ramp to 20 workers (~3.5x baseline) in ~60s under aggressive scaling policy (conservative: 90s)
- Queueing policy: router queues requests up to 30s; after that we return 429s unless you want configurable longer queueing for background jobs
- Backpressure: for streaming requests we prioritize first-token latency by ensuring at least one warm worker is reserved for incoming handshakes (helps meet the ~250ms initial token target)
- Concurrency per worker: tested at ~12–15 concurrent streams per worker before per-worker tail starts to degrade; we used that to size the warm pool

What this means for your SLOs:
- p95: expected to meet <=250ms in the proposed warm-pool config for typical responses (~180 tokens)
- p99: we expect to be around ~800–1200ms depending on token count and queueing during the peak; long responses (600 tokens) will push p99 higher — we can mitigate with batching/kv-cache warmups

Planned benchmark test (what we propose Redwood will run):
1) Synthetic replay of the 1m granularity spike you sent (3x burst profile) for 60 minutes
2) Measure p50/p95/p99 for both first-token and full-response latency, and track token throughput and per-worker CPU/GPU utilization
3) Run warm-pool soak: maintain baseline warm pool for 10 minutes, then inject bursts and observe scale-up time, queueing, and error rates

Next steps:
- If that looks good, confirm a 60-minute slot (we suggested Wed 7/7 or Thu 7/8) and we’ll run the benchmark in a Redwood sandbox tied to your test namespace
- I’ve added an explicit section in the autoscale proposal about queueing thresholds and 429 behavior; see the attached PDF.

I’ll also include a short-run cost estimate for the baseline vs. burst scenarios in the Monday delivery.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-slo-worksheet.xlsx, autoscale-config-proposal.pdf
